subject: VPN burst + egress SLO: quantify targets and next steps
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
To: Alex Chang <alex.chang@fincore.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: VPN burst & egress SLOs — post-demo recapping ask

Alex — thanks for taking time today. Quick recap and proposed asks so we have a single place to track: 

- FinCore targets we heard on the call:
  - 99th percentile tail latency (streaming): <= 250ms per token for 1–2 simultaneous streams per session
  - Sustained throughput: 80 qps for batch (20–32 token average) during trading windows
  - Burst concurrency: up to 220 concurrent model streams for short spikes (5–10m)
  - Egress limit: current private peer has 1 Gbps egress; you indicated we could get to 3 Gbps if procurement approves

- Items we need from your side to finalize qualification:
  1) End-to-end network trace (pcap) of a representative 15-minute trading-period spike (attachment stub requested)
  2) Confirmation of VPN type (IPSec/SSL) and whether NAT is present on customer side
  3) Any proxy/load-balancer (L7) in front of the peer and per-flow connection timeouts

- Redwood proposed next steps:
  - We will draft an initial SLO doc with latency/throughput gates and fallback policy for degraded egress (can route to a warm hosted region)
  - Karthik will run a controlled micro-benchmark against a lab peering with 1 Gbps and 3 Gbps profiles and share results by EOD Fri (7/13)
  - Marissa to align legal/procurement for short-term egress bump options and an uplifted burst SLA

Attachments: placeholder for the 15-min pcap (please send), and a draft SLO spreadsheet (we'll attach v1).

Could you confirm the three items above and share the pcap? If procurement needs a template for egress uplift, loop in procurement@fincore.com and we can share a draft amendment.

Thanks — looking forward to closing the qualification window this week.

— Vanessa Ortiz

Vanessa — appreciate the clear notes. Quick answers and what we attached: 

- Confirmed targets (internal): those latency numbers align with our internal goal for trader-facing flows. We can tolerate up to 400ms 99p during worst-case degradation but prefer <=250ms.
- VPN: IPSec site-to-site, NAT on our edge (one-to-one).
- L7: Yes, we have an L7 proxy (internal HAProxy cluster) with 60s idle timeout; config details attached in the pcap notes.

Attachments: fincore_network_snapshot_20280711.pcap (contains notes in metadata) — SRE dropped a trimmed capture. Also included is a short CSV listing observed concurrent sessions over the morning spike.

Procurement: I looped procurement to start the egress uplift conversation. We can entertain a 3-month trial bump to 3 Gbps. Procurement — can you confirm required PO language and lead time?

SRE note: we observed short-lived TCP retransmits during the spike; happy to run a larger capture if you need more context.

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, Alex Chang <alex.chang@fincore.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Jul 2028 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: VPN burst & egress SLOs — post-demo recapping ask

Thanks Alex — got the trimmed pcap and CSV. Immediate observations from a first-pass micro-benchmark I kicked off in our lab (summary below):

- Lab profiles (1 Gbps vs 3 Gbps peer emulation):
  - 1 Gbps: 99p token latency 270–320ms under sustained 80 qps with 2 streams per session; burst to 200 concurrent streams increases 99p to ~520ms and causes token stalls for ~5–8s at peak
  - 3 Gbps: same sustained load yields 99p 210–240ms; burst to 220 concurrent streams yields 99p ~290–320ms with fewer stalls

- Observed root contributors: TCP queuing on the egress link and L7 proxy connection reuse settings; with short idle timeouts we hit more 3-way handshakes under burst which increases head-of-line latency.

Proposed mitigations we can trial in a POC:
1) Connection pre-warming and connection pooling in the L7 (adjust idle to 300s)
2) Small egress QoS carve for model traffic (priority queuing) — needs network team signoff
3) Short-term burst capacity on Redwood Dedicated via a reserved warm pool to absorb spikes while FinCore procurement bumps link to 3 Gbps

I'll compile a short experiment plan and share expected numbers by EOD today; if FinCore can share a full 15-min raw capture (no trimming) that would help us validate the retransmit patterns.

Karthik
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

- Redwood ops (Karthik): run the two lab profiles (1 Gbps / 3 Gbps) with connection pooling toggled and share the raw results + the SLO draft (slo-proposal-v1.xlsx) by EOD Mon 7/16. Include the expected user-impact curves (latency vs concurrency).

I'll coordinate a 30-minute calibration call after we have the raw capture to agree on acceptance gates (pass/fail criteria).

- Procurement: confirm egress uplift trial (procurement@fincore.com)

Thanks everyone — ping if timing needs to be adjusted.
